inventive_nucleus: A mechanical shutter is used to periodically block the primary LED's light, allowing the reference LED to provide a stable calibration point.
mechanism: The mechanical shutter interacts with the photodetector to control the light intensity measurement.
causal_chain: The primary LED ages over time
The aging of the primary LED affects the calibration
The mechanical shutter blocks the primary LED's light
The reference LED provides a stable light source
The photodetector measures the reference LED light intensity
expected_effect: The biosensor's calibration is maintained within 1% accuracy over a period of 6 months.

predictions.conditions: exposure to extreme temperatures (0-50°C) and humidity (20-80%)
predictions.falsifier: Biosensor calibration accuracy drops below 0.5% after 6 months of continuous use

falsification_tests: Biosensor calibration accuracy drops below 0.5% after 6 months of continuous use

experiment_plan.objective: Investigate the effect of mechanical shutter on biosensor calibration accuracy
independent_variables: exposure to extreme temperatures (0-50°C) and humidity (20-80%)
controls: Reference LED with stable light intensity
procedure: Step 1: Set up the mechanical shutter and reference LED system
Step 2: Expose the biosensor to extreme temperatures (0-50°C) and humidity (20-80%)
Step 3: Measure the biosensor calibration accuracy using the photodetector
